body: The browser's own reason can be cut off at exactly the part that matters. `exitError` puts up to 2,048 bytes of stderr tail (stderrTailBytes) after the `browser could not start: the browser exited (<status>): ` prefix. `requestFailure` then passes the text through `logText`, which keeps the first 1,024 bytes and drops the end. The kept part is the oldest part of the tail; the newest output, usually the fatal line, is discarded. Example: Chromium prints DBus/GPU warnings and then `Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported`. If the warnings fill more than about 970 bytes, the logged cause shows only warnings plus `…` and loses the reason FR-AMZ-BRET-005 asks for. TC-006's multi-line case misses this because it only looks for `stub line`, which appears everywhere in the output. Fix: keep the newest output. For example, drop the start of the tail in `exitError` so that prefix + tail fits in 1,024 bytes (cut on a rune boundary), or set stderrTailBytes below the log budget. Add a test where the last stderr line must appear in the cause after more than 1 KB of earlier output.

Stray editing artifact committed: a fragment of `InformationModal.tsx`, starting at `return (` without its imports or function header. It is not imported, not valid TSX on its own, and not part of the specification. Delete the file.

Leftover from the test stage: a test file that holds only a comment saying it is safe to delete. It adds noise to the `service` package and appears in tests.lock. Remove it, together with its tests.lock entry, wherever the pipeline allows test-file changes.
